name: Pahalgam Tourist Massacre
target: Hindu and Christian tourists in Baisaran Valley, Pahalgam
description: Gunmen attacked a group of tourists in Baisaran Valley near Pahalgam, killing 26 (25 Hindu, 1 Christian). The attack triggered the most severe India-Pakistan crisis since 1971 and led directly to Operation Sindoor. Follow-up: Indian forces reported killing three of the attackers near Dachigam on 28 Jul 2025, and on 30 Sep 2026 reported killing LeT commander Hashim Moosa, named as a key suspect, in Budgam.

name: India Suspends Indus Waters Treaty
target: Bilateral relations and Indus Waters Treaty
description: India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty, closed the Attari-Wagah border crossing, expelled Pakistani diplomats, and reduced High Commission staff. These were the most severe diplomatic measures between the two countries in decades. Update: on 31 Aug 2026 the Court of Arbitration ruled the abeyance impermissible and the treaty in force; India rejected the award on 2 Sep and keeps the treaty in abeyance.

name: Uri Dam Unannounced Water Release
target: Muzaffarabad and downstream Pakistan-administered Kashmir communities
description: India released Uri Dam water without warning, causing flooding in Muzaffarabad in Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Pakistan viewed this as weaponization of water resources under the suspended Indus Waters Treaty.

name: Operation Sindoor: India Strikes 9 Targets
target: Muridke (Markaz-e-Taiba), Bahawalpur, Muzaffarabad, Kotli, Sialkot militant infrastructure
casualties: India claims 100+ militants killed; Pakistan claims 31 civilians killed
description: India launched Operation Sindoor, striking 9 targets across Pakistan-administered Kashmir and Pakistani Punjab. 72 IAF and 42 PAF aircraft engaged in the largest beyond-visual-range air combat on this border. Targets included LeT and JeM facilities.

name: Pakistan Retaliatory Shelling on Poonch
target: Poonch district, J&K — schools, temple, residential areas
description: Pakistan responded to Operation Sindoor with the heaviest mortar and artillery shelling of Poonch since the 1971 war. 31 schools were destroyed and a Sikh temple was damaged. The bombardment targeted civilian areas.

name: Drone and Missile Escalation: S-400 and J-10 First Combat
target: Air defense and strike assets on both sides
casualties: Not tallied separately from overall conflict
description: India deployed S-400 air defense systems in combat for the first time at Adampur air base. Pakistan fielded Chinese-supplied J-10CE fighters with PL-15 missiles. Both sides used armed drones extensively, making this the first drone war between nuclear-armed nations.

name: India Strikes Pakistani Air Bases with BrahMos
target: Nur Khan/Rawalpindi, Rafiqui, Bholari, Mushaf, Sukkur air bases
description: India struck multiple Pakistani air bases with BrahMos and SCALP cruise missiles, marking a significant escalation to strategic military infrastructure targeting. Six PAF personnel were killed at the bases.

name: Pakistan Op Bunyan-um-Marsoos: 34 Indian Targets
target: Adampur, Pathankot, Udhampur air bases; Indian air defense systems
casualties: 1 IAF soldier killed at Udhampur; Pakistan claims S-400 destruction
description: Pakistan launched Operation Bunyan-um-Marsoos, striking 34 Indian military targets including Adampur, Pathankot, and Udhampur air bases. Pakistan claimed destruction of an S-400 battery. A simultaneous cyberattack involved 1.5 million+ intrusion attempts.

name: US-Brokered Ceasefire Ends Four-Day War
target: Cessation of hostilities along LOC and international border
description: A US-brokered ceasefire took effect at 17:00 IST, ending 88 hours of combat. President Trump announced via social media; confirmed by Indian and Pakistani foreign ministries. Saudi Arabia, Iran, UAE, and UK also played roles in de-escalation.

name: Track 2 Talks in Sri Lanka and Thailand
target: Back-channel de-escalation and confidence building
description: Retired Indian and Pakistani diplomats and military officers conducted Track 2 talks in Colombo and Bangkok, the first sustained back-channel engagement since the May 2025 war. Official diplomatic relations remain frozen.

name: Turkey-Saudi-Pakistan Mutual Defense Pact
target: Collective defense framework — attack on one equals attack on all
description: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan signed a mutual defense pact establishing that an attack on any signatory constitutes an attack on all. The agreement includes joint defense projects and counterterrorism operations, representing a significant geopolitical realignment.

name: Pakistan-Administered Kashmir Elections Amid Violence
target: Assembly elections in Pakistan-administered Kashmir
description: Pakistan-administered Kashmir held assembly elections under heavy security with road closures and internet blackouts. At least 24 people were killed in related protests and violence, underscoring the region's volatility one year after the war.

name: Arbitration Court Rules IWT Abeyance Unlawful
target: Indus Waters Treaty; Ratle hydro project on the Chenab
description: The Court of Arbitration at the Permanent Court of Arbitration held that India's April 2025 decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance is not permitted under the treaty, which remains in force, and imposed interim limits on certain concreting at the Ratle project pending the Neutral Expert. India rejected the award on 2 September as from an "illegally constituted" tribunal and said abeyance continues; Pakistan welcomed it.

name: BLA Ambush at Ziarat Cross and Surab VBIED
target: Military convoy at Ziarat Cross; forces in Hajika, Surab (vehicle bomb)
casualties: BLA claims 25 soldiers killed (unverified); military claims ~48 militants killed in follow-up raids
description: The BLA claimed a convoy ambush at Ziarat Cross and a remotely detonated vehicle bomb in Surab (dated 3 or 4 September by different outlets). Pakistani forces responded with operations in Mastung, Sibi, Quetta and Kalat. Casualty figures on both sides are claims, not independently verified.

name: Pakistani and Indian Warships Collide, Arabian Sea
target: PNS Hunain (F-273) and an Indian destroyer on surveillance patrol, North Arabian Sea
description: A Pakistani corvette and an Indian destroyer collided on the evening of 15 September; Indian officials called the Pakistani manoeuvre unsafe and unprofessional, and reports said PNS Hunain returned to Karachi with hull damage. India summoned Pakistan's chargé d'affaires and Pakistan summoned India's; reporting called it the closest military face-off since May 2025. Position approximate (reports place it near Gwadar or ~220 km east of Oman).

name: Suicide and Gun Attack on Kohat Police HQ
target: District police headquarters complex (CTD, Special Branch, mosque), Kohat
casualties: At least 31 killed incl. 16–17 police, 100+ wounded (AFP, 19 Sep); earlier counts 16–24; at least 7 attackers killed
description: Militants struck the Kohat police complex with a suicide blast at its mosque followed by an armed assault, with attackers holding out in the Special Branch section into the next day. The attack was claimed by Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan (some reports name Hafiz Gul Bahadur's faction). Pakistan blamed militants based in Afghanistan, and the attack triggered three rounds of Pakistani airstrikes there.

name: Pakistani Airstrikes Hit Kunar and Paktika
target: Alleged militant hideouts in Nurgal (Kunar) and Barmal (Paktika) districts
casualties: Pakistan claims 28 militants killed; Kabul says 3 civilians of one family killed
description: Pakistan struck what it called militant hideouts in Afghanistan days after the Kohat attack. Afghan officials said the strikes hit Nurgal in Kunar and Barmal in Paktika and killed a villager and two relatives; neither side's figures could be verified. Point placed at Nurgal.

name: Pakistan Downs Eight Afghan Drones at Torkham, Kohat
target: Pakistani positions near Torkham crossing and Kohat
description: Pakistani security sources said air defences shot down eight drones launched from Afghanistan, four near Torkham and four near Kohat, after Pakistani forces hit Taliban positions in the Kurram sector the previous night. Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid denied the drone launches. Single-side security-source reporting.

name: Pakistan Strikes 10 Sites Across Afghanistan
target: Taliban positions in Kandahar, Khost, Paktia and Paktika
casualties: Reports cite at least 40 fighters killed (unverified); Taliban say 4 civilians killed
description: Pakistan's information minister said overnight strikes hit 10 locations in Afghanistan, framed as a response to Taliban drone attacks. The Taliban said four civilians died and vowed to respond. Point placed at Khost.

name: TTP Bomb Attack in Dera Ismail Khan
target: Dera Ismail Khan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
description: A bomb blast in Dera Ismail Khan killed 11 and injured 30; the attack was claimed by the TTP. It came amid the escalation with Kabul that followed the Kohat attack. Single source retrieved (via Wikipedia citation; not fetched directly).

name: LeT Commander Linked to Pahalgam Killed in Budgam
target: Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa, Yousmarg/Doodhpathri area, Budgam district
description: Security forces launched Operation Korag in the Yousmarg area of Budgam on 29 September and said they had killed LeT commander Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa, whom they named among the three key suspects in the April 2025 Pahalgam massacre; his body was recovered on 30 September. Indian authorities had earlier announced that three Pakistani militants behind the attack were killed near Dachigam on 28 July 2025, so how the two operations' identifications relate is not settled in the reporting.

name: Third Round of Pakistani Strikes, Kunar and Helmand
target: Sites Pakistan called terrorist camps in Kunar and Helmand
casualties: Pakistan claims 22 militants killed; Taliban say 9 killed, 11 injured; UNAMA: 10 civilians killed (mostly children), 9 injured
description: Pakistan carried out what it called "planned, calibrated" strikes overnight 30 Sep–1 Oct, the third round since the Kohat attack, which Long War Journal described as a conflict persisting into its third week. UNAMA reported 10 civilian deaths, most of them children. Point placed at Asadabad, Kunar.

name: Emergency and Governor's Rule Imposed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
target: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial government and assembly
description: President Asif Ali Zardari, on federal cabinet advice, imposed an emergency and governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under Articles 232 and 234, citing the security situation and accusing the PTI government of "deliberate disengagement" from counterterrorism. The assembly's powers passed to Parliament amid a PTI march on Islamabad; the provincial government claimed Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was detained, and mobile data was throttled in parts of the province.
